title: The Dark Truth About The Turn of the Screw #Shorts
description:
Evolution does not optimize for happiness — The Turn of the Screw shows exactly where that breaks. The Turn of the Screw is an 1898 gothic horror novella by Henry James which first appeared in serial format in Collier's Weekly from January 27 to April 16, 1898. On October 7, 1898, it was Collected in The Two Magics, published by Macmillan in New York City and Heinemann in London.

The selfish-gene reading of The Turn of the Screw makes it less romantic and far more precise. According to scholar Terry Heller, most early reviewers saw the novel as a formidable piece of Gothic fiction. An early review of The Turn of the Screw was in The New York Times Saturday Review of Books and Art, stating it was worthy of being compared to Robert Louis Stevenson's Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde (1886).
